generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The removal of `assertAcked` means that the test will no longer assert that the update settings operation is acknowledged. This could lead to scenarios where the method proceeds even if the cluster settings update fails silently, potentially causing subsequent tests to fail or behave unpredictably. Additionally, the introduction of `.get(TimeValue.timeValueSeconds(30))` makes the operation synchronous and waits for a response within 30 seconds, which increases test execution time and introduces potential bottlenecks. This change ensures that the settings update operation is completed before the method proceeds but no longer checks if the update was acknowledged, leading to silent failures that are difficult to diagnose and increased variability in test performance.

review_comment:
I am a bit confused.

This says zen2 is default, however the actual constant value is `zen`:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bcfbf000748b538884087623113682165abcb92d/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/discovery/DiscoveryModule.java#L63-L72

Anyways, even if it is using the different discovery type, is it safe to ignore ack?
The property is still used in couple of places as for 7.17, such as https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/bcfbf000748b538884087623113682165abcb92d/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/gateway/Gateway.java#L44

`zen` means Zen2, there is no option in 7.x to use the legacy discovery type.

Yes I believe this is safe, or at least it's no less safe than other things related to upgrading from 6.x. Which was never completely safe anyway.
